run.userPrompt:
A technology company still earns a third of its profit from a legacy product it stopped actively developing years ago; the replacement product is stronger but lacks a few niche features that the most loyal legacy customers depend on. Maintenance costs and security exposure on the old platform grow every year, and the engineers who understand it are approaching retirement. Some large customers threaten to switch vendors entirely if forced to migrate.

Plan the end-of-life and migration program for the legacy product. Set the sunset timeline and support policy, decide which niche capabilities must be rebuilt versus retired, design migration incentives and tooling for each customer tier, and prepare the retention plan for the customers most likely to defect during the transition.

agentRuns.systemPrompt: [137 chars] You will be presented with a business problem. Analyze the situation and propose solutions. Provide a complete, well-structured response.
agentRuns.userPrompt: [15,673 chars] [PREVIOUS WORK] **The Architecture of Recovery: A Surgical Margin-Reclamation Strategy**  The blunt price increases failed because they treated pricing as a finance exercise—uniform cost-pass-through—

agentResponses.content:
**The Controlled Sunset: A Legacy Product Migration & Retention Architecture** Treating this as a product problem—announcing an end-of-life date and publishing a migration guide—will fail. The legacy platform contributes one-third of profit, its remaining engineers possess irreplaceable tacit knowledge, and the replacement is incomplete only at the edges. This is a **revenue continuity, liability containment, and knowledge-transfer crisis**. The goal is not merely to decommission code, but to *transplant* the profit pool before the engineering brain drain and security exposure make it impossible. This strategy replaces a blunt forced migration with a **controlled demolition**: a tiered, financially instrumented, and capability-triaged transition that compresses the timeline to minimize risk, while using commercial and technical architecture to make migration less painful than defection. --- ### 1. Strategic Doctrine: “Harvest, Bridge, Migrate, Retain” Publish these principles internally. They govern every trade-off among Product, Engineering, Sales, and Legal. | Principle | Operational Rule | |-----------|------------------| | **Risk-Adjusted Profit Over GAAP Profit** | The legacy product’s stated margin ignores security liability, engineering attrition, and opportunity cost. Every quarter of delay consumes 1.5–2x the apparent “profit” in hidden risk. | | **Time Compression Over Gradualism** | The sunsetting clock is set by the retirement dates of the 3–5 engineers who understand the core stack, not by customer comfort. The program is bounded by a hard 24-month operational horizon. | | **Migration is a Service, Not a Release** | Customers do not resist the new product; they resist *transition cost*. The SKU is not software licenses but “business continuity as a project.” | | **Niche Features Are Not Product Debt** | Do not rebuild the entire legacy surface area. Triage niche capabilities by customer revenue concentration and build cost. Some gaps are filled by partners, some by temporary bridges, and some are allowed to retire. | | **Retention Through Architecture, Not Desperation** | For customers threatening defection, the counter-offer is never a perpetual legacy license. It is a co-developed migration path, a managed-service bridge, or a dignified exit package that preserves the commercial relationship. | --- ### 2. The Sunset Timeline & Support Policy: The Hard Stop A fuzzy timeline guarantees that customers stall, engineers retire, and the security surface area widens. The timeline below is **non-negotiable** and communicated simultaneously to all customers. | Milestone | Date | Policy | |-----------|------|--------| | **T-0: Announcement & End of Sale (EOS)** | Month 0 | All new commercial sales and renewals >12 months cease immediately. Existing customers may renew once for a final 12-month term with a signed Migration Commitment Letter. | | **T+6: End of Engineering Support (EOES)** | Month 6 | No new features, no bug fixes, no performance patches. Engineering shifts 100% to migration tooling and replacement-platform parity. | | **T+12: End of Security Patches (EOSP)** | Month 12 | Critical (CVSS ≥8.0) vulnerabilities patched only. All other security issues receive workarounds or risk-acceptance documentation. | | **T+18: End of Life (EOL)** | Month 18 | All support terminates. No patches, no hotlines, no documentation updates. Customers still running the platform sign a release of liability to continue operating unpatched. | | **T+18 to T+24: Extended Migration Security (EMS)** | Months 18–24 | *Tier 1 customers only.* A punitive-cost option (5× historical maintenance) providing only critical security patches, contingent on proof of >80% migration completion. This is a safety net, not a destination. | **The “Tiger Team” Engineering Lock** Immediately upon announcement, identify the 3–5 legacy engineers approaching retirement. Offer retention bonuses of 1.5–2.0× annualized salary vesting at T+18 in exchange for: * Full-time migration-tooling and documentation sprints (not legacy maintenance). * Reverse-shadowing by two mid-level engineers per domain. * Signed-off runbooks for every undocumented workaround and hot-fix in production. --- ### 3. Capability Triage: The Rebuild-Bridge-Retire-Partner Framework The replacement product is stronger at the core. The blockers are niche. Evaluate every missing capability against **customer revenue concentration** and **build complexity**. | Bucket | Criteria | Action | |--------|----------|--------| | **Rebuild** | Missing feature is used by customers representing >25% of legacy revenue; build estimate <6 months; aligns with replacement-platform roadmap. | Native development on the new platform. Launch as a “migration release” before T+12. Fund by reallocating legacy maintenance budget. | | **Bridge** | Critical to 1–3 large accounts; high complexity; needed only during transition. | Build an API adapter, compatibility shim, or scripted workaround that runs alongside the new platform. Sunset the bridge 12 months after the last customer migrates. | | **Partner** | Vertical or niche need outside core competency; viable ISV ecosystem. | Offer development grants and co-marketing to 1–2 ISVs to build certified apps on the new platform. Transition support burden to partner. | | **Retire** | Used by <10% of revenue base; high maintenance burden; workaround exists or can be documented. | Formal deprecation at T-0. Provide data-export tools and a “capability mapping” guide showing how 80% of the use case is achieved via native replacement features. No engineering investment. | **The Triage Governance Rule:** No capability is rebuilt unless a named Tier 1 or Tier 2 customer has signed a Migration Commitment Letter contingent on its delivery. Do not build on speculation. --- ### 4. Customer Tiering & Migration Architecture One migration playbook does not fit all. Segment by revenue, technical complexity, and churn risk, then tailor the commercial and technical package. | Tier | Profile | Migration Incentive & Commercial Model | Tooling & Delivery | Support Model | |------|---------|----------------------------------------|--------------------|---------------| | **Tier 1: Strategic Anchors** | Top 20% of legacy revenue; complex on-prem or custom deployments; highest defection threat. | **Success-Based Migration:** 100% license-fee holiday for Year 1 on the new platform. Post-migration, pricing locked at legacy rates for 24 months. If missing niche features are rebuilt, customer co-funds 25% of dev cost in exchange for 12-month exclusivity. | Dedicated Migration Pod (Solutions Architect + two engineers). Custom ETL scripts. Bi-directional sync bridge for 90-day parallel run. Executive sponsor from your C-suite meets their CIO quarterly. | White-glove TAM; 24/7 war room during cutover. | | **Tier 2: Core Installed Base** | Middle 60%; moderate customization; sticky but price-sensitive. | **Bridge Licensing:** 50–75% first-year discount. Fixed-fee professional services package ($X per instance). Training credits and certification vouchers for their admins. | Self-service Migration Wizard (assessed, configured, executed via UI). Standardized REST APIs for data export/import. Migration playbook with runbook templates. | Professional Services lead; community forum; office hours. | | **Tier 3: Long Tail** | Bottom 20%; low revenue or low complexity; often “set and forget.” | **Cloud-Only Conversion:** Offer a new SaaS-only tier at a price point below legacy maintenance. Freemium data-import tool. Partner-led migration rebates (you pay the partner, not the customer). | Automated instance scanner and importer. Video tutorial library. Chatbot-guided setup. | Community support only; partner channel handles touch. | **The Parallel-Run Protocol** For Tier 1 and complex Tier 2 customers, mandate a 30- to 90-day parallel operation. The bridge tooling (above) syncs data bi-directionally so they can revert without data loss. This de-risks the cutover and reduces political resistance. --- ### 5. The Retention & Defection Defense Protocol Even with incentives, some customers will threaten to leave. Classify them by pathology, not just size, and deploy targeted retention plays. #### Defector Personas & Countermeasures | Persona | Diagnosis | Retention Play | |---------|-----------|----------------| | **The Feature Hostage** | “We cannot move until Niche Capability X exists natively.” | **Joint Development Covenant:** If Feature X is in the Rebuild bucket, the customer pays 25–50% of build cost and receives a 12-month exclusive license plus input on UX. If in the Bridge bucket, deliver the temporary adapter free of charge for the parallel-run period. | | **The Integration Prison** | “We have 40,000 lines of custom code and 12 downstream systems on your legacy APIs.” | **The Escape Consultant:** Fund a dedicated integration architect (from your PS team or a named partner) to audit and refactor their custom layer. Provide a legacy-to-new API translation gateway so their downstream systems require minimal changes. | | **The Political Defector** | “We are considering Competitor Y regardless of your migration path.” | **The Commercial Innovation Play:** Offer an outcome-based contract for the first 18 months—payment is contingent on uptime or performance benchmarks on the new platform. If they still leave, offer the **Dignified Exit Package**: free data liberation, API access for 24 months post-departure, and a joint case study framing the migration as their strategic choice. Preserves future re-entry and references. | | **The Complacent Institution** | “We will move when we are ready—maybe in 2027.” | **The Escalating Risk Conversation:** At T+6, present a joint risk memo (signed by your CISO and their CIO) documenting the growing security exposure. At T+12, require a signed Risk Acceptance Letter to renew. Make inaction administratively painful inside their own organization. | **The “Stay vs. Leave” Economics Conversation** For any Tier 1 customer threatening defection, conduct a facilitated Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) workshop comparing three scenarios over 36 months: 1. **Migrate to your new platform** (including your incentives). 2. **Migrate to Competitor Y** (data migration, retraining, re-integration—typically 1.5–2× your path). 3. **Stay on legacy past EOL** (unpatched security risk, no engineering support, eventual emergency migration at crisis pricing). In most cases, Scenario 1 is the rational choice; the workshop simply makes the internal business case for your champion. --- ### 6. Engineering & Knowledge Wind-Down The human capital risk is as severe as the customer risk. | Initiative | Action | |------------|--------| | **The Documentation Blitz** | Do not document the legacy product generally. Document it *surgically* for migration: dependency maps, data-schema translations, known workaround scripts, and failure modes. Target: 200 hours of video capture and runbook authorship per retiring engineer. | | **Reverse Mentoring Pairs** | Pair each legacy engineer with two mid-level engineers. The junior owns the migration tool; the senior critiques. Knowledge transfers through building, not shadowing. | | **Code Archaeology Sprint** | Use static analysis and runtime telemetry to identify which legacy modules are actually exercised by the current install base. Deprioritize documenting dead code. Focus engineering on the 20% of the codebase touching 80% of customers. | | **Migration Tooling as Product** | Elevate the migration wizard, API bridge, and data importer to first-class product status with a dedicated PM. These tools are the primary delivery vehicle; their UX determines churn more than the replacement product’s feature set. | --- ### 7. Governance: The Sunset War Room Establish a permanent, cross-functional command structure with veto power over any initiative that extends the legacy timeline. | Body | Composition | Cadence | Authority | |------|-------------|---------|-----------| | **Sunset Steering Committee** | CRO, CTO, CPO, General Counsel, Head of Customer Success | Weekly | Sets policy; approves all rebuild/retire decisions; owns the P&L reallocation from legacy maintenance to migration investment. | | **Customer Risk Register** | Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering | Weekly | Maintains the Top 20 defection-risk accounts. Each account has a named “Retention Owner” and a documented play (see Section 5). | | **Capability Triage Board** | Product Management, Engineering Lead, Sales Engineering | Bi-weekly | Rules on Rebuild vs. Bridge vs. Retire. No work begins without a signed Migration Commitment Letter from a paying customer. | | **Migration Velocity Dashboard** | PMO, Finance | Monthly | Tracks: % of legacy revenue migrated, $ support cost trending down, engineering headcount on legacy vs. new, and customer NPS by tier. | **The “No Lifeline” Rule** No individual sales rep or account executive is permitted to promise extended legacy support, custom engineering, or delayed EOL dates. All exceptions must be approved by the Sunset Steering Committee and the General Counsel. A single unauthorized promise to a Tier 1 account can collapse the entire timeline. --- ### 8. Implementation Roadmap: 24-Month Sequence | Phase | Timeline | Actions | |-------|----------|---------| | **Phase 1: Triage & Announcement** | Months 0–3 | • Lock the Triage Board; publish the 24-month timeline to all customers.
• Stop new legacy sales; offer final 12-month renewal with Migration Commitment Letter.
• Form the Tiger Team; begin documentation blitz and reverse mentoring.
• Segment full customer base into Tiers 1–3; load the Risk Register. | | **Phase 2: Tooling & Parity Build** | Months 4–9 | • Rebuild approved niche capabilities on new platform.
• Launch Migration Wizard (Tier 2) and dedicated Migration Pods (Tier 1).
• End all legacy engineering except critical security patches (T+6).
• Begin professional services engagements with Tier 1; pilot parallel-run bridges. | | **Phase 3: Migration Acceleration** | Months 10–15 | • Migrate 60% of Tier 3 via self-service and partners.
• Complete 40% of Tier 2 via fixed-fee PS packages.
• Cutover first wave of Tier 1 with executive-sponsored parallel runs.
• Publish partner-built apps for retired capabilities. | | **Phase 4: Hard Landing & Harvest** | Months 16–21 | • Enforce EOL at Month 18; transition remaining holdouts to EMS (Tier 1 only) or risk-acceptance.
• Migrate final Tier 1 accounts.
• Retire the legacy codebase; reassign Tiger Team to replacement-product R&D or customer-success roles.
• Conduct post-mortem and institutionalize “end-of-life as a capability” for future product cycles. | | **Phase 5: Stabilization** | Months 22–24 | • Harmonize pricing for migrated customers onto standard schedules.
• Capture case studies from successful migrations.
• Dissolve Sunset War Room; transfer ongoing support to standard CS operations. | --- ### 9. Financial Reallocation: Funding the Transition The legacy product’s profit should not be harvested as EBITDA. Redirect it: * **Legacy Maintenance Budget → Migration Investment Fund:** Reallocate 70% of legacy engineering and support spend to migration tooling, bridge development, and Tier 1 professional services subsidies. * **Retention Bonuses → Accrued Liability:** Book the Tiger Team retention bonuses as a recognized liability so Finance does not treat the legacy profit as distributable cash. * **Customer Incentives → CAC Bridge:** Treat first-year discounts and license holidays as a Customer Acquisition Cost against the new platform. The payback period is 18–24 months through standard renewal pricing and lower support costs. --- **Bottom Line:** You are not sunsetting a product; you are performing **profit transplantation** from a decaying platform to a growing one. The only variables are whether you control the timeline or the timeline controls you, and whether you migrate the customer relationship or watch it defect. Speed, surgical capability triage, and tiered migration architecture are the difference between a controlled sunset and a corporate cardiac event.
